text: This man just swallowed his gum, and it's sliding down his throat.
Kids are told it stays in your belly for seven years.
In his stomach, acid strips off the sugar and flavor.
But the gum base is made of rubber, and his body can't break it down.
So it slides along through about twenty feet of gut.
And in a few days, it comes out the other end, almost the same as it went in.
Doctors who look inside people almost never find gum older than a week.
The twist: two kids who swallowed gum every day got a giant gum ball stuck inside.
So one piece is fine. A pack a day is not.
And that's what really happens when you swallow gum.
